Empty draws a solid rectangle of `color`. A picture made at run time (`render.captureTexture`, `render.textureFromPNG`) works here too: use its `id` ("runtime:3"; docs/SCRIPTING.md, "Render"). So does the live picture of a camera: "target:<name>" for the Camera whose `renderTarget` is that name (docs/RENDERING.md, "Render targets"). |
| `slice` | vec4 | `[0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0]` | 9-slice borders in TEXTURE pixels [left, top, right, bottom]. The four corners are drawn unscaled (1 texture pixel = 1 design pixel), the edges stretch along one axis and the centre along both, so one small image gives panels of any size. [0, 0, 0, 0] (default) stretches the whole image. When the widget is smaller than left + right (or top + bottom) the borders shrink proportionally. |
| `tooltip` | json | `null` | The hint that shows next to the pointer after it rests on the widget for `ui.tooltipDelay` seconds (0.5 by default) and goes away when the pointer moves, a button is pressed or another widget is reached. null (default) = none. A string is one line of text, or a localization key (docs/LOCALIZATION.md: a string that is a key of the current language is replaced by its translation, anything else is shown as written). An object {"title": text, "lines": [text or {"text", "color"}], "args": {...}} has a title and body lines; every text may be a key, `args` fills the {placeholders} of the keys, and the tooltip follows a language change while it shows. A widget without a tooltip of its own uses its parent Panel's, so one on a Panel covers its children. It is styled by the `ui.tooltip` section of factoria.json, placed beside the pointer and kept on the screen, and off while the last input was a touch (unless `ui.tooltipOnTouch` is true). A script that returns the text when it shows registers it with ui.setTooltip(entity, () => content) instead. docs/MENUS.md, "Tooltips". (since 0.3.0) |
| `draggable` | json | `null` | Lets the player drag the widget with the mouse, a finger or a gamepad cursor (ui.setPointer). null or false (default) = not draggable; true = draggable with the default slop; an object {"payload": any JSON, "slop": pixels} sets what the drag carries (default null) and how far the pointer must move after the press before the drag starts (default 6, 0 to 100). A press that is released before the slop is a normal click. When the drag starts the widget is no longer pressed, the click the release would make is swallowed, a tooltip hides, and ui.on("dragStart" \| "dragOver" \| "drop" \| "dragCancel") report it with the widget as source; a press on a child that is not draggable itself drags the nearest draggable ancestor. Slider and TextField keep their own pointer handling and ignore it. docs/MENUS.md, "Drag and drop". (since 0.3.0) |
| `mirror` | bool | `true` | true (default): in a right-to-left language the widget is mirrored when `ui.mirrorRtl` is on (it is, by default, when i18n.direction is rtl): its anchor.x, pivot.x and position.x flip, so it sits where its mirror image about the middle of the screen would, with the same size; a Toggle's box is at the right of its label, a Slider fills from its right end, a Button's icon changes side, and a Panel with direction auto runs its rows right to left. Text, Sprite and Shape2D below the widget are mirrored with it. false: the widget (and everything below it) stays where it is written, for what is not text-like: a map, a joystick, a clock face. A CameraView changes side with the layout but its picture is never mirrored. Does nothing in a left-to-right language or with ui.mirrorRtl off (docs/LOCALIZATION.md, "Right to left"). (since 0.3.0) |
| `font` | asset (font) | `""` | Font of the label: project path of a .ttf, empty = the built-in font (same values as Text.font). |
| `key` | string | `""` | Localization key, e.g. "menu.play" (docs/LOCALIZATION.md). Empty (default) = not translated. With a key, the runtime writes the translation into the widget's own text: Button.text, Toggle.label, Slider.label, or TextField.placeholder (never TextField.text, which is what the player typed). It does so when a scene or prefab loads, every frame and when the language changes, so that field is overwritten at run time while `key` is set. A key that no string table has keeps the text written in the field and logs one warning. It is a TRANSLATION key, not a hotkey: a Button has no field for a keyboard key or pad button. To press a button with one, declare an input action in factoria.json ("input") and read it with input.pressed in a script. (since 0.2.0) |
| `keyArgs` | json | `{}` | Values for the {placeholders} of `key`, an object of name -> string or number: {"score": 12} fills "Score: {score}" (and `count` picks the form of a plural entry). Set it once from a script (`entity.set("Text", { keyArgs: { score } })` or `scene.set_component`) instead of rewriting the text every frame: the engine formats the translation with them when the text is localized, when the args change and when the language changes, so a language switch keeps them. Empty (default) = no arguments. Ignored while `key` is empty. (since 0.3.0) |
| `fontSize` | float | `24.0` | Label glyph height in design pixels. Range 1.0..4096.0. |
| `maxTextScale` | float | `0.0` | > 0: the player's text size (ui.textScale) stops growing this text at this scale, so a heading or a round button label does not outgrow its place: 1.3 means it is drawn at most 1.3 times its fontSize however big the option is. It only limits growth: at a text size below the cap it is drawn at the player's size. 0 (default) = no cap. Measuring (autoSize, layout, ui.measureText, ui.rectOf) and drawing use the same capped size. Range 0.0..3.0. (since 0.3.0) |
| `textColor` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0]` | Label colour. |
| `accentColor` | color | `[1.0,0.76,0.2,1.0]` | Colour of the focus ring, the slider fill and knob, the toggle check mark and the text caret. |
| `interactable` | bool | `true` | false: the widget is drawn at half alpha and is never hovered, focused or clicked, so it sends no ui events. A focused widget that becomes non-interactable loses focus. |
| `autoFocus` | bool | `false` | Focus rule: nothing takes keyboard / gamepad focus by itself, except that when NOTHING is focused the first widget with autoFocus = true (reading order: top, then left) takes it. Mark the first item of each menu; HUD buttons then stay out of gamepad play (Space / A must never click a HUD button). When the focused widget disappears (inactive, destroyed, not interactable) autoFocus applies again. When every visible autoFocus widget has interactable = false (a greyed-out buy button), the first interactable widget in reading order takes the focus instead, so the gamepad is never left with nothing focused. |
| `focused` | bool | `false` | Runtime: true while the widget has keyboard / gamepad focus. Written by the UI every frame; move focus with ui.focus(entity). Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `hovered` | bool | `false` | Runtime: the pointer (mouse or first touch) is over this widget, the top-most visible interactable one. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `pressed` | bool | `false` | Runtime: the pointer is held down on this widget. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `label` | string | `""` | Text at the left (or above the track with labelAbove); empty gives the track the extra room. |
| `maxWidth` | float | `0.0` | > 0 wraps the label at this width in design pixels (like Text.maxWidth); 0 = one line. With autoSize the slider grows taller for the extra lines. Range 0.0..100000.0. (since 0.3.0) |
| `labelAbove` | bool | `false` | true: the label is drawn above the track on the slider's full width (wrapping at maxWidth or the width) and the track, knob and value sit in a row of 28 px at the bottom, so a long label does not squeeze the track. The slider needs a height of the label plus 28 px (autoSize adds it). false (default): the label is in the left 35%. (since 0.3.0) |
| `autoSize` | bool | `false` | true: the widget is at least its design `size` and grows to fit its label at the current text size (ui.textScale) and language, re-laid out when either changes (needs no script). Width and height are set every frame, so writing `size` while this is on sets the NEW design size; turn it off to keep a size. A Button, Toggle or Slider label wraps at its `maxWidth` (and the widget grows taller); with no maxWidth the label does not wrap. autoSize makes room for the full-size label, so autoShrink only works on a widget that does not grow. false (default): the widget keeps its size and a big label sticks out of it (Button labels are clipped). (since 0.2.0) |
| `autoShrink` | bool | `false` | true: when the text does not fit its box at the current text size (ui.textScale) and language, the font is made smaller until it does, never under `minFontSize` (so a German label in a fixed button stays inside at 200 % text, and a long translation is smaller instead of cut). It is decided every frame from the laid-out size, with no script. If it still does not fit at minFontSize it is drawn there and ui.overflowed(id) is true. false (default): the size is never reduced. (since 0.3.0) |
| `minFontSize` | float | `10.0` | autoShrink floor in design pixels, before ui.textScale (the floor is minFontSize times the player's text size, capped by maxTextScale, so the accessibility setting keeps working). Never above fontSize. Range 1.0..4096.0. (since 0.3.0) |
| `markup` | bool | `false` | true: the text reads tags: [b]bold[/b], [i]italic[/i] (the italic face of the font: factoria.json text.fonts "italic", or the built-in family's own, e.g. builtin:serif), [c:good]coloured[/c] (a name of factoria.json text.colors, a built-in colour name or #rrggbb) and [icon:fish] (a picture of text.icons, drawn inline as tall as the line); [[ is a literal [. Wrapping, alignment, maxWidth, autoShrink and ui.measureText all work on the visible characters, so the tags take no room. A tag the engine does not know is shown as written, `factoria validate` and ui.markupProblems(text) report it. false (default): the string is drawn as it is, so a [ in it is only a [. A run colour replaces the colour of the text and keeps its opacity. Docs: docs/TEXT.md, "Rich text". (since 0.3.0) |
| `bold` | bool | `false` | true: the whole text is bold. It uses the bold face the project gives the font (factoria.json text.fonts); a font with none is emboldened by the engine, and `factoria validate` suggests adding one. builtin:serif, builtin:hand and builtin:display bring real bold or italic faces of their own. [b] in markup does the same for a part of the text. false (default): regular weight. (since 0.3.0) |
| `value` | float | `0.5` | Current value, always within [min, max] and snapped to `step` by the UI. Scripts may write it; no event is sent for a write. |
| `min` | float | `0.0` | Smallest value. |
| `max` | float | `1.0` | Largest value. |
| `step` | float | `0.1` | Keyboard / gamepad increment, and the grid the value is snapped to (also when dragging). 0 = continuous: keys move (max - min) / 20 per press and dragging is not snapped. Range 0.0..1000000.0. |
| `showValue` | bool | `true` | Draw the value at the right. Without `format`: "60%" when min is 0 and max is 1, else the number with up to 2 decimals. |
| `format` | string | `""` | Pattern of the shown value, e.g. "{v}%" or "{v:1}x". {v} is the value with up to 2 decimals (trailing zeros dropped), {v:N} the value with exactly N decimals (0 to 6), {percent} the value times 100 rounded to a whole number (a 0.3..1 opacity slider shows 30%..100% with "{percent}%"; {percent} does not depend on min and max). A doubled brace writes one brace; any other {name} is drawn as it is, so a typo is visible. Empty = the default of showValue. It sizes autoSize and draws in the value column only; ui.state `value` stays the number. Use formatKey for a pattern per language. (since 0.3.0) |
| `formatKey` | string | `""` | Localization key whose translation is the pattern, written into `format` like `key` writes the label ("slider.percent": "{v} %" in French). "" = none. A key no table has is reported once and `format` stays as it is. (since 0.3.0) |

### Interactable

Since 0.4.0.

Makes this entity, whatever it is made of (sprites, shapes, text, children), a widget that joins the same focus, navigation and events as Button, Toggle and Slider: hover, press, click, focus, the arrow keys / d-pad (spatial navigation), ui_next / ui_previous (Tab), ui_submit / ui_cancel, Panel.modal scopes, game.click, ui.widgetAt and the ui.* commands find it by id. The hit area is `size` (a rectangle in the entity's local space) or, with size 0, the bounds of the entity and its children; in world space it is projected through the camera that draws there, so it follows parents that move, scale or rotate (a turning page, a swaying sign). An entity with screen-space visuals is a screen-space widget. An entity that is also a Button, Toggle, Slider, TextField, Panel or other UI-box component keeps that role and its Interactable is ignored. Draw the look with ordinary children and InteractableVisual (show, hide or tint per state). Events (ui.on): click (button), change (toggle / slider, value), focus, blur, hover (value true = entered, false = left), press and release (value true = released over it). A world-space widget under a screen-space widget (or outside a modal Panel) is not reached.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | enum: button \\| toggle \\| slider | `"button"` | button: a click or ui_submit sends ui.click {id}. toggle: it flips `on` and sends ui.change {id, value: bool}. slider: dragging along the area or left / right (down / up with axis y) sets `value` and sends ui.change {id, value: number}. |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` | false: the Disabled state. It is never hovered, focused, pressed or clicked and sends no events; a focused one loses focus. Visuals with when/disabled show. |
| `autoFocus` | bool | `false` | Same rule as Button.autoFocus: when NOTHING is focused the first widget with autoFocus (reading order of their areas on the screen) takes the keyboard / gamepad focus. Mark the first item of each menu. |
| `focusOnHover` | bool | `false` | true: the pointer entering the widget moves the focus to it (once per entry, so the arrow keys still move it away). A widget that appears (or turns on) under a resting pointer counts as an entry. false (default, like the built-in widgets): the focus moves on a press. |
| `size` | vec2 | `[0.0,0.0]` | Hit area [w, h] in the entity's LOCAL units, y up (screen space: UI units), so it scales and turns with the entity and its parents. [0, 0] (default) = the bounding box (in the entity's own frame) of the visuals of the entity and its active children, not counting InteractableVisual entities that Show/Hide with the state, a slider's knob and fill, and children that are Interactables themselves; an entity with no visuals then has no area and cannot be hit. |
| `offset` | vec2 | `[0.0,0.0]` | Centre of the explicit area [x, y] from the entity origin, in local units. Ignored when size is [0, 0]. |
| `space` | enum: auto \\| world \\| screen | `"auto"` | auto (default): screen space when the entity or one of its children draws in screen space or has a UI box, else world space. world: the area is projected through the camera. screen: the area is in screen space (UI units; the anchor and safeArea of the entity's own screen-space Text, Sprite or Shape2D, else the top-left corner of the screen). |
| `on` | bool | `false` | Toggle: the value. Scripts may write it; no event is sent for a write. Visuals with when on / off follow it. |
| `value` | float | `0.0` | Slider: the value, always within [min, max] and snapped to `step` by the UI. Scripts may write it; no event is sent for a write. `knob` and `fill` follow it every frame. |
| `min` | float | `0.0` | Slider: the smallest value. |
| `max` | float | `1.0` | Slider: the largest value. |
| `step` | float | `0.0` | Slider: the keyboard / gamepad increment and the grid the value snaps to (also when dragging). 0 = continuous: keys move (max - min) / 20 per press. Range 0.0..1000000.0. |
| `axis` | enum: x \\| y | `"x"` | Slider: the track runs along the area's local x (min at the left end, max at the right) or local y (min at the bottom, max at the top). The area is the track: its length along the axis is the travel of the knob. |
| `knob` | entity |  | Slider: id of the entity moved along the track so that it sits at the value (only its local position along `axis` is set, in the frame of its own parent: make it a child of this entity). Empty = none. |
| `fill` | entity |  | Slider: id of the entity whose local scale along `axis` becomes the fraction (value - min) / (max - min), and whose position along the axis is the start of the track. Give it a pivot at its start (a Shape2D or Sprite with pivot [0, 0.5]) and the size of the whole track. Empty = none. |
| `label` | string | `""` | Accessibility label, what ui.state reports as `text` and the read-aloud recipe speaks. Empty = the text of the first Text among the entity and its children. Overwritten by the translation while `key` is set. |
| `key` | string | `""` | Localization key for `label` (docs/LOCALIZATION.md), like Button.key. Empty = not translated. |
| `keyArgs` | json | `{}` | Values for the {placeholders} of `key`, an object of name -> string or number: {"score": 12} fills "Score: {score}" (and `count` picks the form of a plural entry). Set it once from a script (`entity.set("Text", { keyArgs: { score } })` or `scene.set_component`) instead of rewriting the text every frame: the engine formats the translation with them when the text is localized, when the args change and when the language changes, so a language switch keeps them. Empty (default) = no arguments. Ignored while `key` is empty. |
| `focused` | bool | `false` | Runtime: has keyboard / gamepad focus. Written by the UI every frame; move focus with ui.focus(entity). Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `hovered` | bool | `false` | Runtime: the pointer (mouse or first touch) is over it and it is the top-most widget there. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `pressed` | bool | `false` | Runtime: the pointer is held down on it. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `state` | enum: normal \\| hover \\| pressed \\| focused \\| disabled | `"normal"` | Runtime: the one state the visuals show: disabled (enabled is false), else pressed, else hover, else focused, else normal. Written by the UI every frame. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |

### InteractableVisual

Since 0.4.0.

Makes this entity follow the state of an Interactable with no script. Show: the entity is active only while `when` holds (a highlight on hover, a check mark when a toggle is on, a pressed sprite). Tint: the colour of its Sprite, Shape2D or Text (the first one it has) is set from the state every frame. Put it on a child of the Interactable or give `target`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | entity |  | Id of the Interactable to follow. Empty (default) = the nearest ancestor that has an Interactable. |
| `mode` | enum: show \\| tint | `"show"` | show: the entity is active only while `when` holds. tint: its colour follows the state (the colours below). |
| `when` | enum: always \\| normal \\| hover \\| pressed \\| focused \\| highlighted \\| disabled \\| on \\| off | `"hover"` | Show only. always: always active. normal: neither hovered, pressed, focused nor disabled. hover, pressed, focused: that flag is set (a hovered and focused widget shows both). highlighted: hovered OR focused (one look for the pointer and the keyboard / gamepad, so they never disagree). disabled: enabled is false. on / off: a toggle's `on` is true / false. |
| `normal` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0]` | Tint: colour in the normal state. |
| `hover` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0]` | Tint: colour while hovered (and not pressed). |
| `pressed` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0]` | Tint: colour while pressed. |
| `focused` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0]` | Tint: colour while focused (and not hovered or pressed). |
| `disabled` | color | `[0.5,0.5,0.5,0.6]` | Tint: colour while the Interactable is not enabled. |

### TextField

Since 0.1.6.

Single-line text input. While focused it appends the typed characters (Input text), Backspace removes the last one (it repeats while held) and Enter submits. There is no caret movement: the caret stays at the end. Events: ui.change {id, value} on every edit (one per frame), ui.submit {id, value} on Enter. Left / right do nothing in a TextField and Space types a space (ui_submit is ignored).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | vec2 | `[320.0,48.0]` | Size [w, h] in UI units: design pixels, drawn `ui.scale` times as big (the interface scale; 1 by default). The default depends on the kind (Button 240 x 56, Toggle 240 x 40, Slider 320 x 40, TextField 320 x 48, Panel and ScrollList 320 x 240, TouchStick 200 x 200, TouchButton 96 x 96, Captions 960 x 180, Video 640 x 360, Chart 480 x 200, CameraView 320 x 240). A Panel with fit = true recomputes it every frame (within its minSize and maxSize). |
| `pivot` | vec2 | `[0.5,0.5]` | Which point of the widget sits on the position: [0.5, 0.5] = its centre (default), [0, 1] = top-left corner, [1, 0] = bottom-right. Same meaning as Shape2D.pivot in screen space: +Y is down on screen but pivot [0, 1] is still the visual top-left. So the pivot counts Y UP while `anchor` counts Y DOWN: anchor [0.5, 1] with pivot [0.5, 0] puts the widget's bottom edge on the bottom of the screen, and with pivot [0.5, 1] it hangs below the screen (docs/MENUS.md, "Anchors and pivots"). Layout does not care about the pivot of its children. |
| `anchor` | vec2 | `[0.0,0.0]` | Screen point the position is relative to, as a fraction of the screen: [0, 0] top-left (default), [1, 0] top-right, [0.5, 0.5] centre. Anchor [0.5, 0.5] with position [0, 0] centres the widget on any aspect ratio. The interface scale (`ui.scale`) never moves the anchor point: a widget anchored to a corner stays in it. The anchor of the widget itself is used, not its parent's: children of a Panel normally keep anchor [0, 0] and are placed by the Panel's layout. |
| `safeArea` | bool | `false` | Screen space only. true: the anchor names a point of the SAFE area, the screen minus the notch, rounded corners and system bars of a phone (screen.safeArea in scripts), instead of the whole screen: anchor [0, 0] is the top-left corner of the safe area, [1, 1] its bottom-right. Keeps HUD and buttons out of the notch. On a screen without cutouts (desktop, most tablets) it changes nothing. Default false (true on TouchStick and TouchButton). (since 0.2.0) |
| `layer` | int | `200` | Draw order of the background; higher is on top. Defaults to 200, above HUD Text (layer 100). The label draws at layer + 1 and the focus ring at layer + 2. Pointer hit-testing follows the same order: the highest layer, then the latest entity, under the pointer is the hovered widget. |
| `color` | color | `[0.16,0.18,0.24,0.92]` | Background colour, multiplied with `texture` when there is one. Hovered widgets are brightened, pressed ones darkened, non-interactable ones drawn at half alpha. Accepts [r,g,b,a], "#rrggbb" or a name. |
| `texture` | asset (texture) | `""` | Optional background image (project path), drawn as a 9-slice (see `slice`) with nearest-neighbour sampling, so pixel art stays crisp. Empty draws a solid rectangle of `color`. A picture made at run time (`render.captureTexture`, `render.textureFromPNG`) works here too: use its `id` ("runtime:3"; docs/SCRIPTING.md, "Render"). So does the live picture of a camera: "target:<name>" for the Camera whose `renderTarget` is that name (docs/RENDERING.md, "Render targets"). |
| `slice` | vec4 | `[0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0]` | 9-slice borders in TEXTURE pixels [left, top, right, bottom]. The four corners are drawn unscaled (1 texture pixel = 1 design pixel), the edges stretch along one axis and the centre along both, so one small image gives panels of any size. [0, 0, 0, 0] (default) stretches the whole image. When the widget is smaller than left + right (or top + bottom) the borders shrink proportionally. |
| `tooltip` | json | `null` | The hint that shows next to the pointer after it rests on the widget for `ui.tooltipDelay` seconds (0.5 by default) and goes away when the pointer moves, a button is pressed or another widget is reached. null (default) = none. A string is one line of text, or a localization key (docs/LOCALIZATION.md: a string that is a key of the current language is replaced by its translation, anything else is shown as written). An object {"title": text, "lines": [text or {"text", "color"}], "args": {...}} has a title and body lines; every text may be a key, `args` fills the {placeholders} of the keys, and the tooltip follows a language change while it shows. A widget without a tooltip of its own uses its parent Panel's, so one on a Panel covers its children. It is styled by the `ui.tooltip` section of factoria.json, placed beside the pointer and kept on the screen, and off while the last input was a touch (unless `ui.tooltipOnTouch` is true). A script that returns the text when it shows registers it with ui.setTooltip(entity, () => content) instead. docs/MENUS.md, "Tooltips". (since 0.3.0) |
| `draggable` | json | `null` | Lets the player drag the widget with the mouse, a finger or a gamepad cursor (ui.setPointer). null or false (default) = not draggable; true = draggable with the default slop; an object {"payload": any JSON, "slop": pixels} sets what the drag carries (default null) and how far the pointer must move after the press before the drag starts (default 6, 0 to 100). A press that is released before the slop is a normal click. When the drag starts the widget is no longer pressed, the click the release would make is swallowed, a tooltip hides, and ui.on("dragStart" \| "dragOver" \| "drop" \| "dragCancel") report it with the widget as source; a press on a child that is not draggable itself drags the nearest draggable ancestor. Slider and TextField keep their own pointer handling and ignore it. docs/MENUS.md, "Drag and drop". (since 0.3.0) |
| `mirror` | bool | `true` | true (default): in a right-to-left language the widget is mirrored when `ui.mirrorRtl` is on (it is, by default, when i18n.direction is rtl): its anchor.x, pivot.x and position.x flip, so it sits where its mirror image about the middle of the screen would, with the same size; a Toggle's box is at the right of its label, a Slider fills from its right end, a Button's icon changes side, and a Panel with direction auto runs its rows right to left. A CameraView changes side with the layout but its picture is never mirrored. Does nothing in a left-to-right language or with ui.mirrorRtl off (docs/LOCALIZATION.md, "Right to left"). (since 0.3.0) |
| `font` | asset (font) | `""` | Font of the label: project path of a .ttf, empty = the built-in font (same values as Text.font). |
| `key` | string | `""` | Localization key, e.g. "menu.play" (docs/LOCALIZATION.md). Empty (default) = not translated. With a key, the runtime writes the translation into the widget's own text: Button.text, Toggle.label, Slider.label, or TextField.placeholder (never TextField.text, which is what the player typed). It does so when a scene or prefab loads, every frame and when the language changes, so that field is overwritten at run time while `key` is set. A key that no string table has keeps the text written in the field and logs one warning. It is a TRANSLATION key, not a hotkey: a Button has no field for a keyboard key or pad button. To press a button with one, declare an input action in factoria.json ("input") and read it with input.pressed in a script. (since 0.2.0) |
| `keyArgs` | json | `{}` | Values for the {placeholders} of `key`, an object of name -> string or number: {"score": 12} fills "Score: {score}" (and `count` picks the form of a plural entry). Set it once from a script (`entity.set("Text", { keyArgs: { score } })` or `scene.set_component`) instead of rewriting the text every frame: the engine formats the translation with them when the text is localized, when the args change and when the language changes, so a language switch keeps them. Empty (default) = no arguments. Ignored while `key` is empty. (since 0.3.0) |
| `fontSize` | float | `24.0` | Label glyph height in design pixels. Range 1.0..4096.0. |
| `maxTextScale` | float | `0.0` | > 0: the player's text size (ui.textScale) stops growing this text at this scale, so a heading or a round button label does not outgrow its place: 1.3 means it is drawn at most 1.3 times its fontSize however big the option is. It only limits growth: at a text size below the cap it is drawn at the player's size. 0 (default) = no cap. Measuring (autoSize, layout, ui.measureText, ui.rectOf) and drawing use the same capped size. Range 0.0..3.0. (since 0.3.0) |
| `textColor` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0]` | Label colour. |
| `accentColor` | color | `[1.0,0.76,0.2,1.0]` | Colour of the focus ring, the slider fill and knob, the toggle check mark and the text caret. |
| `interactable` | bool | `true` | false: the widget is drawn at half alpha and is never hovered, focused or clicked, so it sends no ui events. A focused widget that becomes non-interactable loses focus. |
| `autoFocus` | bool | `false` | Focus rule: nothing takes keyboard / gamepad focus by itself, except that when NOTHING is focused the first widget with autoFocus = true (reading order: top, then left) takes it. Mark the first item of each menu; HUD buttons then stay out of gamepad play (Space / A must never click a HUD button). When the focused widget disappears (inactive, destroyed, not interactable) autoFocus applies again. When every visible autoFocus widget has interactable = false (a greyed-out buy button), the first interactable widget in reading order takes the focus instead, so the gamepad is never left with nothing focused. |
| `focused` | bool | `false` | Runtime: true while the widget has keyboard / gamepad focus. Written by the UI every frame; move focus with ui.focus(entity). Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `hovered` | bool | `false` | Runtime: the pointer (mouse or first touch) is over this widget, the top-most visible interactable one. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `pressed` | bool | `false` | Runtime: the pointer is held down on this widget. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `text` | string | `""` | The text, UTF-8. Scripts may write it; no event is sent for a write. |
| `placeholder` | string | `""` | Hint drawn at half alpha while `text` is empty. |
| `maxLength` | int | `64` | Longest text, in characters (code points). 0 = unlimited. Range 0.0..1000000.0. |
| `caret` | bool | `false` | Runtime: the caret is in the visible half of its blink (a 1 second cycle of the UI's own unscaled clock; it restarts visible on every edit). Drawn only while focused. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |

### ScrollList

Since 0.1.6.

Scrolling container: its children are stacked in a column (aligned left, packed at the top) at -scroll, and everything drawn by them and their descendants (widgets, Text, Sprite, Shape2D) is CLIPPED to the list's rectangle. The mouse wheel over the list scrolls it (the innermost list under the pointer) when it has more content than it shows; that wheel is then consumed: input.mouse.wheel reads 0 for the frame and ui.wheelConsumed is true. Focusing a widget inside scrolls just enough to show it.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | vec2 | `[320.0,240.0]` | Size [w, h] in UI units: design pixels, drawn `ui.scale` times as big (the interface scale; 1 by default). The default depends on the kind (Button 240 x 56, Toggle 240 x 40, Slider 320 x 40, TextField 320 x 48, Panel and ScrollList 320 x 240, TouchStick 200 x 200, TouchButton 96 x 96, Captions 960 x 180, Video 640 x 360, Chart 480 x 200, CameraView 320 x 240). A Panel with fit = true recomputes it every frame (within its minSize and maxSize). |
| `pivot` | vec2 | `[0.5,0.5]` | Which point of the widget sits on the position: [0.5, 0.5] = its centre (default), [0, 1] = top-left corner, [1, 0] = bottom-right. Same meaning as Shape2D.pivot in screen space: +Y is down on screen but pivot [0, 1] is still the visual top-left. So the pivot counts Y UP while `anchor` counts Y DOWN: anchor [0.5, 1] with pivot [0.5, 0] puts the widget's bottom edge on the bottom of the screen, and with pivot [0.5, 1] it hangs below the screen (docs/MENUS.md, "Anchors and pivots"). Layout does not care about the pivot of its children. |
| `anchor` | vec2 | `[0.0,0.0]` | Screen point the position is relative to, as a fraction of the screen: [0, 0] top-left (default), [1, 0] top-right, [0.5, 0.5] centre. Anchor [0.5, 0.5] with position [0, 0] centres the widget on any aspect ratio. The interface scale (`ui.scale`) never moves the anchor point: a widget anchored to a corner stays in it. The anchor of the widget itself is used, not its parent's: children of a Panel normally keep anchor [0, 0] and are placed by the Panel's layout. |
| `safeArea` | bool | `false` | Screen space only. true: the anchor names a point of the SAFE area, the screen minus the notch, rounded corners and system bars of a phone (screen.safeArea in scripts), instead of the whole screen: anchor [0, 0] is the top-left corner of the safe area, [1, 1] its bottom-right. Keeps HUD and buttons out of the notch. On a screen without cutouts (desktop, most tablets) it changes nothing. Default false (true on TouchStick and TouchButton). (since 0.2.0) |
| `layer` | int | `200` | Draw order of the background; higher is on top. Defaults to 200, above HUD Text (layer 100). The label draws at layer + 1 and the focus ring at layer + 2. Pointer hit-testing follows the same order: the highest layer, then the latest entity, under the pointer is the hovered widget. |
| `color` | color | `[0.16,0.18,0.24,0.92]` | Background colour, multiplied with `texture` when there is one. Hovered widgets are brightened, pressed ones darkened, non-interactable ones drawn at half alpha. Accepts [r,g,b,a], "#rrggbb" or a name. |
| `texture` | asset (texture) | `""` | Optional background image (project path), drawn as a 9-slice (see `slice`) with nearest-neighbour sampling, so pixel art stays crisp. Empty draws a solid rectangle of `color`. A picture made at run time (`render.captureTexture`, `render.textureFromPNG`) works here too: use its `id` ("runtime:3"; docs/SCRIPTING.md, "Render"). So does the live picture of a camera: "target:<name>" for the Camera whose `renderTarget` is that name (docs/RENDERING.md, "Render targets"). |
| `slice` | vec4 | `[0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0]` | 9-slice borders in TEXTURE pixels [left, top, right, bottom]. The four corners are drawn unscaled (1 texture pixel = 1 design pixel), the edges stretch along one axis and the centre along both, so one small image gives panels of any size. [0, 0, 0, 0] (default) stretches the whole image. When the widget is smaller than left + right (or top + bottom) the borders shrink proportionally. |
| `tooltip` | json | `null` | The hint that shows next to the pointer after it rests on the widget for `ui.tooltipDelay` seconds (0.5 by default) and goes away when the pointer moves, a button is pressed or another widget is reached. null (default) = none. A string is one line of text, or a localization key (docs/LOCALIZATION.md: a string that is a key of the current language is replaced by its translation, anything else is shown as written). An object {"title": text, "lines": [text or {"text", "color"}], "args": {...}} has a title and body lines; every text may be a key, `args` fills the {placeholders} of the keys, and the tooltip follows a language change while it shows. A widget without a tooltip of its own uses its parent Panel's, so one on a Panel covers its children. It is styled by the `ui.tooltip` section of factoria.json, placed beside the pointer and kept on the screen, and off while the last input was a touch (unless `ui.tooltipOnTouch` is true). A script that returns the text when it shows registers it with ui.setTooltip(entity, () => content) instead. docs/MENUS.md, "Tooltips". (since 0.3.0) |
| `draggable` | json | `null` | Lets the player drag the widget with the mouse, a finger or a gamepad cursor (ui.setPointer). null or false (default) = not draggable; true = draggable with the default slop; an object {"payload": any JSON, "slop": pixels} sets what the drag carries (default null) and how far the pointer must move after the press before the drag starts (default 6, 0 to 100). A press that is released before the slop is a normal click. When the drag starts the widget is no longer pressed, the click the release would make is swallowed, a tooltip hides, and ui.on("dragStart" \| "dragOver" \| "drop" \| "dragCancel") report it with the widget as source; a press on a child that is not draggable itself drags the nearest draggable ancestor. Slider and TextField keep their own pointer handling and ignore it. docs/MENUS.md, "Drag and drop". (since 0.3.0) |
| `mirror` | bool | `true` | true (default): in a right-to-left language the widget is mirrored when `ui.mirrorRtl` is on (it is, by default, when i18n.direction is rtl): its anchor.x, pivot.x and position.x flip, so it sits where its mirror image about the middle of the screen would, with the same size; a Toggle's box is at the right of its label, a Slider fills from its right end, a Button's icon changes side, and a Panel with direction auto runs its rows right to left. Text, Sprite and Shape2D below the widget are mirrored with it. false: the widget (and everything below it) stays where it is written, for what is not text-like: a map, a joystick, a clock face. A CameraView changes side with the layout but its picture is never mirrored. Does nothing in a left-to-right language or with ui.mirrorRtl off (docs/LOCALIZATION.md, "Right to left"). (since 0.3.0) |
| `spacing` | float | `8.0` | Gap in design pixels between children. Range 0.0..10000.0. |
| `padding` | vec4 | `[8.0,8.0,8.0,8.0]` | Space [left, top, right, bottom] between the list's edge and its children. |
| `scroll` | float | `0.0` | Runtime: pixels scrolled from the top. Scripts may write it; it is clamped to [0, content height - inner height] every frame. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `scrollSpeed` | float | `40.0` | Pixels scrolled per mouse-wheel notch. Range 0.0..10000.0. |
| `fill` | bool | `false` | true: when the parent is a Panel with layout column, `size.y` is set every frame to the height the other children leave. In a Panel with `fit` that is the screen height (minus the safe-area insets) minus the panel's padding, the gaps and the other children, so the panel ends exactly as tall as the screen at most (never below 64 px; if the other children do not leave that, the panel is taller than the screen and warns). In a Panel without fit it is the panel's own inner height minus the others. Several fill lists share the room equally. Ignored when the parent is not a column Panel. `size.x` is yours. (since 0.2.0) |
| `shrink` | bool | `false` | true: like `fill`, but the list is only as tall as its content (padding, children and gaps) when that is less than the room the other children leave, so inside a `fit` Panel a short list makes a short panel and a long one stops at the screen height and scrolls. The room is computed as for `fill` (it needs a parent Panel with layout column; ignored otherwise; never below 64 px). `fill` and `shrink` together: `fill` wins. Several shrink lists share the room: each takes what it needs, and a list that needs more than an equal share takes what the shorter ones leave. `size.x` is yours. (since 0.3.0) |

### TouchStick

Since 0.2.0.

On-screen analog stick for phones and tablets (docs/MOBILE.md): a disc in `color` with a knob that follows the finger. A finger that lands on it moves a stick of the TOUCH PAD, a virtual gamepad the action bindings read like a real one, so actions bound to GamepadLeftStickLeft/Right/Up/Down (or the right stick) work with no change to the game; the default ui_* actions include the left stick, so it also walks menus. Full tilt is the edge of the disc (half the shorter side); the pad deadzone (input.deadzone) applies like on a real stick. That finger is the stick's until it lifts, even outside the disc: it is not in input.touches, the Touch binding or the mouse. Several fingers work at once (a stick and buttons). Defaults: 200 x 200, inside the safe area, shown only while the player uses touch (touchOnly).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | vec2 | `[200.0,200.0]` | Size [w, h] in UI units: design pixels, drawn `ui.scale` times as big (the interface scale; 1 by default). The default depends on the kind (Button 240 x 56, Toggle 240 x 40, Slider 320 x 40, TextField 320 x 48, Panel and ScrollList 320 x 240, TouchStick 200 x 200, TouchButton 96 x 96, Captions 960 x 180, Video 640 x 360, Chart 480 x 200, CameraView 320 x 240). A Panel with fit = true recomputes it every frame (within its minSize and maxSize). |
| `pivot` | vec2 | `[0.5,0.5]` | Which point of the widget sits on the position: [0.5, 0.5] = its centre (default), [0, 1] = top-left corner, [1, 0] = bottom-right. Same meaning as Shape2D.pivot in screen space: +Y is down on screen but pivot [0, 1] is still the visual top-left. So the pivot counts Y UP while `anchor` counts Y DOWN: anchor [0.5, 1] with pivot [0.5, 0] puts the widget's bottom edge on the bottom of the screen, and with pivot [0.5, 1] it hangs below the screen (docs/MENUS.md, "Anchors and pivots"). Layout does not care about the pivot of its children. |
| `anchor` | vec2 | `[0.0,0.0]` | Screen point the position is relative to, as a fraction of the screen: [0, 0] top-left (default), [1, 0] top-right, [0.5, 0.5] centre. Anchor [0.5, 0.5] with position [0, 0] centres the widget on any aspect ratio. The interface scale (`ui.scale`) never moves the anchor point: a widget anchored to a corner stays in it. The anchor of the widget itself is used, not its parent's: children of a Panel normally keep anchor [0, 0] and are placed by the Panel's layout. |
| `safeArea` | bool | `true` | Screen space only. true: the anchor names a point of the SAFE area, the screen minus the notch, rounded corners and system bars of a phone (screen.safeArea in scripts), instead of the whole screen: anchor [0, 0] is the top-left corner of the safe area, [1, 1] its bottom-right. Keeps HUD and buttons out of the notch. On a screen without cutouts (desktop, most tablets) it changes nothing. Default false (true on TouchStick and TouchButton). |
| `layer` | int | `200` | Draw order of the background; higher is on top. Defaults to 200, above HUD Text (layer 100). The label draws at layer + 1 and the focus ring at layer + 2. Pointer hit-testing follows the same order: the highest layer, then the latest entity, under the pointer is the hovered widget. |
| `color` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,0.2]` | Background colour, multiplied with `texture` when there is one. Hovered widgets are brightened, pressed ones darkened, non-interactable ones drawn at half alpha. Accepts [r,g,b,a], "#rrggbb" or a name. |
| `texture` | asset (texture) | `""` | Optional background image (project path), drawn as a 9-slice (see `slice`) with nearest-neighbour sampling, so pixel art stays crisp. Empty draws a solid rectangle of `color`. A picture made at run time (`render.captureTexture`, `render.textureFromPNG`) works here too: use its `id` ("runtime:3"; docs/SCRIPTING.md, "Render"). So does the live picture of a camera: "target:<name>" for the Camera whose `renderTarget` is that name (docs/RENDERING.md, "Render targets"). |
| `slice` | vec4 | `[0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0]` | 9-slice borders in TEXTURE pixels [left, top, right, bottom]. The four corners are drawn unscaled (1 texture pixel = 1 design pixel), the edges stretch along one axis and the centre along both, so one small image gives panels of any size. | `stick` | enum: left \\| right | `"left"` | Which stick of the touch pad it moves. |
| `knobColor` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,0.6]` | Colour of the knob, a disc 45% as wide as the stick. |
| `touchOnly` | bool | `true` | true (default): drawn and listed as visible only while the last input came from a finger (input.lastDevice "touch"; a phone or tablet starts that way), so it hides when the player picks up a gamepad or a keyboard and comes back on the next touch. A finger landing on it always works. false: always drawn (desktop previews, screenshots, tests). |

### TouchButton

Since 0.2.0.

| `button` | enum: A \\| B \\| X \\| Y \\| Start \\| Back \\| Guide \\| DpadLeft \\| DpadRight \\| DpadUp \\| DpadDown \\| LeftShoulder \\| RightShoulder \\| LeftThumb \\| RightThumb | `"A"` | The pad button it holds down: actions bound to "Gamepad" + this name (GamepadA, GamepadDpadUp...) fire. Bind the game's actions to pad buttons in factoria.json input.actions to use them. |
| `text` | string | `""` | Label centred on the button, e.g. "A" or "Jump". Empty (default) draws none. |
| `key` | string | `""` | Localization key, e.g. "touch.jump" (docs/LOCALIZATION.md). Empty (default) = not translated. With a key, the runtime writes the translation into `text` when a scene loads, every frame and when the language changes. A key that no string table has keeps `text` and logs one warning. (since 0.3.0) |
| `keyArgs` | json | `{}` | Values for the {placeholders} of `key`, an object of name -> string or number: {"score": 12} fills "Score: {score}" (and `count` picks the form of a plural entry). Set it once from a script (`entity.set("Text", { keyArgs: { score } })` or `scene.set_component`) instead of rewriting the text every frame: the engine formats the translation with them when the text is localized, when the args change and when the language changes, so a language switch keeps them. Empty (default) = no arguments. Ignored while `key` is empty. (since 0.3.0) |
| `font` | asset (font) | `""` | Font of the label: project path of a .ttf, empty = the built-in font. |
| `fontSize` | float | `32.0` | Label glyph height in design pixels. Range 1.0..4096.0. |
| `autoShrink` | bool | `false` | true: when the text does not fit its box at the current text size (ui.textScale) and language, the font is made smaller until it does, never under `minFontSize` (so a German label in a fixed button stays inside at 200 % text, and a long translation is smaller instead of cut). It is decided every frame from the laid-out size, with no script. If it still does not fit at minFontSize it is drawn there and ui.overflowed(id) is true. false (default): the size is never reduced. (since 0.3.0) |
| `minFontSize` | float | `10.0` | autoShrink floor in design pixels, before ui.textScale (the floor is minFontSize times the player's text size, capped by maxTextScale, so the accessibility setting keeps working). Never above fontSize. Range 1.0..4096.0. (since 0.3.0) |
| `maxTextScale` | float | `0.0` | > 0: the player's text size (ui.textScale) stops growing this text at this scale, so a heading or a round button label does not outgrow its place: 1.3 means it is drawn at most 1.3 times its fontSize however big the option is. It only limits growth: at a text size below the cap it is drawn at the player's size. 0 (default) = no cap. Measuring (autoSize, layout, ui.measureText, ui.rectOf) and drawing use the same capped size. Range 0.0..3.0. (since 0.3.0) |
| `markup` | bool | `false` | true: the text reads tags: [b]bold[/b], [i]italic[/i] (the italic face of the font: factoria.json text.fonts "italic", or the built-in family's own, e.g. builtin:serif), [c:good]coloured[/c] (a name of factoria.json text.colors, a built-in colour name or #rrggbb) and [icon:fish] (a picture of text.icons, drawn inline as tall as the line); [[ is a literal [. Wrapping, alignment, maxWidth, autoShrink and ui.measureText all work on the visible characters, so the tags take no room. A tag the engine does not know is shown as written, `factoria validate` and ui.markupProblems(text) report it. false (default): the string is drawn as it is, so a [ in it is only a [. A run colour replaces the colour of the text and keeps its opacity. Docs: docs/TEXT.md, "Rich text". (since 0.3.0) |
| `bold` | bool | `false` | true: the whole text is bold. It uses the bold face the project gives the font (factoria.json text.fonts); a font with none is emboldened by the engine, and `factoria validate` suggests adding one. builtin:serif, builtin:hand and builtin:display bring real bold or italic faces of their own. [b] in markup does the same for a part of the text. false (default): regular weight. (since 0.3.0) |
| `textColor` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,0.9]` | Label colour. |
| `touchOnly` | bool | `true` | true (default): drawn and listed as visible only while the last input came from a finger (input.lastDevice "touch"; a phone or tablet starts that way), so it hides when the player picks up a gamepad or a keyboard and comes back on the next touch. A finger landing on it always works. false: always drawn (desktop previews, screenshots, tests). |
| `pressed` | bool | `false` | Runtime: a finger holds the button. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `shown` | bool | `false` | Runtime: drawn this frame (see touchOnly). Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |

### Captions

Since 0.2.0.

The subtitles of the game (docs/TEXT.md, "Captions"): draws the lines that `audio.play(path, { caption })` and `ui.caption(text, seconds)` put on the caption list, the newest `maxLines` of them, at the bottom of this entity's rectangle on a background that hugs the text. Text is drawn like Text: it follows ui.textScale, the localization font chain and right-to-left languages. Put ONE per scene (or in a persistent HUD). Without any Captions entity captions are still tracked (game.captions() in tests lists them) but nothing is drawn, and the log says so once. An inactive Captions entity draws nothing either: that is how a "Subtitles" option turns them off. Defaults: bottom centre of the safe area, 960 x 180, over a dark background.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | vec2 | `[960.0,180.0]` | Size [w, h] in UI units: design pixels, drawn `ui.scale` times as big (the interface scale; 1 by default). The default depends on the kind (Button 240 x 56, Toggle 240 x 40, Slider 320 x 40, TextField 320 x 48, Panel and ScrollList 320 x 240, TouchStick 200 x 200, TouchButton 96 x 96, Captions 960 x 180, Video 640 x 360, Chart 480 x 200, CameraView 320 x 240). A Panel with fit = true recomputes it every frame (within its minSize and maxSize). |
| `pivot` | vec2 | `[0.5,0.0]` | Which point of the widget sits on the position: [0.5, 0.5] = its centre (default), [0, 1] = top-left corner, [1, 0] = bottom-right. Same meaning as Shape2D.pivot in screen space: +Y is down on screen but pivot [0, 1] is still the visual top-left. So the pivot counts Y UP while `anchor` counts Y DOWN: anchor [0.5, 1] with pivot [0.5, 0] puts the widget's bottom edge on the bottom of the screen, and with pivot [0.5, 1] it hangs below the screen (docs/MENUS.md, "Anchors and pivots"). Layout does not care about the pivot of its children. |
| `anchor` | vec2 | `[0.5,1.0]` | Screen point the position is relative to, as a fraction of the screen: [0, 0] top-left (default), [1, 0] top-right, [0.5, 0.5] centre. Anchor [0.5, 0.5] with position [0, 0] centres the widget on any aspect ratio. The interface scale (`ui.scale`) never moves the anchor point: a widget anchored to a corner stays in it. The anchor of the widget itself is used, not its parent's: children of a Panel normally keep anchor [0, 0] and are placed by the Panel's layout. |
| `safeArea` | bool | `true` | Screen space only. true: the anchor names a point of the SAFE area, the screen minus the notch, rounded corners and system bars of a phone (screen.safeArea in scripts), instead of the whole screen: anchor [0, 0] is the top-left corner of the safe area, [1, 1] its bottom-right. Keeps HUD and buttons out of the notch. On a screen without cutouts (desktop, most tablets) it changes nothing. Default false (true on TouchStick and TouchButton). |
| `layer` | int | `200` | Draw order of the background; higher is on top. Defaults to 200, above HUD Text (layer 100). The label draws at layer + 1 and the focus ring at layer + 2. Pointer hit-testing follows the same order: the highest layer, then the latest entity, under the pointer is the hovered widget. |
| `color` | color | `[0.0,0.0,0.0,0.7]` | Background colour, multiplied with `texture` when there is one. Hovered widgets are brightened, pressed ones darkened, non-interactable ones drawn at half alpha. Accepts [r,g,b,a], "#rrggbb" or a name. |
| `texture` | asset (texture) | `""` | Optional background image (project path), drawn as a 9-slice (see `slice`) with nearest-neighbour sampling, so pixel art stays crisp. Empty draws a solid rectangle of `color`. A picture made at run time (`render.captureTexture`, `render.textureFromPNG`) works here too: use its `id` ("runtime:3"; docs/SCRIPTING.md, "Render"). So does the live picture of a camera: "target:<name>" for the Camera whose `renderTarget` is that name (docs/RENDERING.md, "Render targets"). |
| `slice` | vec4 | `[0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0]` | 9-slice borders in TEXTURE pixels [left, top, right, bottom]. The four corners are drawn unscaled (1 texture pixel = 1 design pixel), the edges stretch along one axis and the centre along both, so one small image gives panels of any size. [0, 0, 0, 0] (default) stretches the whole image. When the widget is smaller than left + right (or top + bottom) the borders shrink proportionally. |
| `tooltip` | json | `null` | The hint that shows next to the pointer after it rests on the widget for `ui.tooltipDelay` seconds (0.5 by default) and goes away when the pointer moves, a button is pressed or another widget is reached. null (default) = none. A string is one line of text, or a localization key (docs/LOCALIZATION.md: a string that is a key of the current language is replaced by its translation, anything else is shown as written). An object {"title": text, "lines": [text or {"text", "color"}], "args": {...}} has a title and body lines; every text may be a key, `args` fills the {placeholders} of the keys, and the tooltip follows a language change while it shows. A widget without a tooltip of its own uses its parent Panel's, so one on a Panel covers its children. It is styled by the `ui.tooltip` section of factoria.json, placed beside the pointer and kept on the screen, and off while the last input was a touch (unless `ui.tooltipOnTouch` is true). A script that returns the text when it shows registers it with ui.setTooltip(entity, () => content) instead. docs/MENUS.md, "Tooltips". (since 0.3.0) |
| `draggable` | json | `null` | Lets the player drag the widget with the mouse, a finger or a gamepad cursor (ui.setPointer). null or false (default) = not draggable; true = draggable with the default slop; an object {"payload": any JSON, "slop": pixels} sets what the drag carries (default null) and how far the pointer must move after the press before the drag starts (default 6, 0 to 100). A press that is released before the slop is a normal click. When the drag starts the widget is no longer pressed, the click the release would make is swallowed, a tooltip hides, and ui.on("dragStart" \| "dragOver" \| "drop" \| "dragCancel") report it with the widget as source; a press on a child that is not draggable itself drags the nearest draggable ancestor. Slider and TextField keep their own pointer handling and ignore it. docs/MENUS.md, "Drag and drop". (since 0.3.0) |
| `mirror` | bool | `true` | true (default): in a right-to-left language the widget is mirrored when `ui.mirrorRtl` is on (it is, by default, when i18n.direction is rtl): its anchor.x, pivot.x and position.x flip, so it sits where its mirror image about the middle of the screen would, with the same size; a Toggle's box is at the right of its label, a Slider fills from its right end, a Button's icon changes side, and a Panel with direction auto runs its rows right to left. Text, Sprite and Shape2D below the widget are mirrored with it. false: the widget (and everything below it) stays where it is written, for what is not text-like: a map, a joystick, a clock face. A CameraView changes side with the layout but its picture is never mirrored. Does nothing in a left-to-right language or with ui.mirrorRtl off (docs/LOCALIZATION.md, "Right to left"). (since 0.3.0) |
| `maxLines` | int | `3` | How many captions show at once. When more are on the list the oldest are not drawn (they stay on the list until their sound ends or their seconds run out). Range 1.0..16.0. |
| `padding` | vec4 | `[16.0,8.0,16.0,8.0]` | Space [left, top, right, bottom] between the edge of the background and the text. |
| `font` | asset (font) | `""` | Font of the captions: project path of a .ttf, empty = the built-in font (same values as Text.font). |
| `fontSize` | float | `28.0` | Glyph height in design pixels, before ui.textScale. Range 1.0..4096.0. |
| `textColor` | color | `[1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0]` | Colour of the caption text. |
| `speakerColor` | color | `[1.0,0.82,0.35,1.0]` | Colour of the speaker's name, drawn before the line ("Mara:"). Captions without a speaker have no name. |
| `align` | enum: left \\| center \\| right \\| start \\| end | `"center"` | Where the block of captions sits inside the rectangle's width, and how the lines align in it. Same values as Text.align: start / end follow the language (start = right in Arabic or Hebrew). |
| `spacing` | float | `4.0` | Gap in design pixels between two captions. Range 0.0..1000.0. |
| `lines` | json | `[]` | Runtime: what is drawn now, [{text, speaker}] oldest first, at most `maxLines`. Written by the engine every frame from the caption list; do not edit it. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |

### Video

Since 0.3.0.

A video on the screen (docs/MENUS.md, "Studio intro"): plays an .mpg file (MPEG-1 video with MP2 sound, the same decoder on every platform) in this entity's rectangle, the way an image fills a widget. Convert any other video with `factoria call assets.import '{"source":"intro.mp4"}'` (needs ffmpeg: `factoria setup ffmpeg`). The sound plays on the mixer bus `bus` at `volume`. Time follows the game clock: the video pauses with the game (time.scale 0) and a headless run shows the same pictures at the same times as a windowed one. Control it from a script with `entity.video.play()`, `pause()`, `stop()`, `seek(seconds)` and read `time`, `duration`, `playing`; when it reaches its end the game event `video.ended` ({id, path}) fires once (`entity.video.on("ended", fn)`). The picture is decoded on the CPU: keep videos at most about 1280 x 720. Defaults: 640 x 360, a black background (shown as bars where the picture does not fill the rectangle), starts playing at once.

|---|---|---|---|

A Panel with fit = true recomputes it every frame (within its minSize and maxSize). |

So the pivot counts Y UP while `anchor` counts Y DOWN: anchor [0.5, 1] with pivot [0.5, 0] puts the widget's bottom edge on the bottom of the screen, and with pivot [0.5, 1] it hangs below the screen (docs/MENUS.md, "Anchors and pivots"). Layout does not care about the pivot of its children. |

The anchor of the widget itself is used, not its parent's: children of a Panel normally keep anchor [0, 0] and are placed by the Panel's layout. |

Keeps HUD and buttons out of the notch. On a screen without cutouts (desktop, most tablets) it changes nothing. Default false (true on TouchStick and TouchButton). |

Pointer hit-testing follows the same order: the highest layer, then the latest entity, under the pointer is the hovered widget. |

| `texture` | asset (texture) | `""` | Optional background image (project path), drawn as a 9-slice (see `slice`) with nearest-neighbour sampling, so pixel art stays crisp. Empty draws a solid rectangle of `color`. A picture made at run time (`render.captureTexture`, `render.textureFromPNG`) works here too: use its `id` ("runtime:3"; docs/SCRIPTING.md, "Render"). So does the live picture of a camera: "target:<name>" for the Camera whose `renderTarget` is that name (docs/RENDERING.md, "Render targets"). |

| `path` | asset (video) | `""` | Project path of the video (.mpg). Changing it opens the new file (and starts it again when `autoplay`). A file that is missing or is not MPEG-1 video is logged once and the entity draws only its background. |
| `autoplay` | bool | `true` | true (default): `playing` becomes true as soon as the file is open. false: it waits for `entity.video.play()` or `playing = true`, showing the first picture. |
| `loop` | bool | `false` | true: at the end the video starts over from the beginning, picture and sound (no `video.ended` event). false: it stops on its last picture and fires `video.ended`. |

| `ended` | bool | `false` | Runtime: true once the video reached its end (never while `loop`); false again after a seek or a restart. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `time` | float | `0.0` | Runtime: seconds into the video, 0 .. duration. Assign to seek (the picture and the sound jump there). Range 0.0..1000000.0. Runtime-only (not saved). |
| `duration` | float | `0.0` | Runtime: length of the video in seconds; 0 while the file is not open. Read-only. Runtime-only (not saved). |

### CameraView

Since 0.3.0.

A 3D (or 2D) view inside the UI (docs/MENUS.md, "A camera inside the UI"): draws the camera named by `camera` into this entity's rectangle, so an item turning on a stage, a character portrait or a map lives in a menu with the clipping of a ScrollList, the `layer` order, the right-to-left mirroring and the modal Panel of any widget. The camera is rendered into an image of the size of the rectangle (its aspect follows it; Camera.viewport is ignored) before the frame's UI is drawn, then that image is drawn in the rectangle. Give the camera primary = false, or it also draws in the main view; the camera and the widget must both be active. The background is drawn at `layer`, the picture at `layer` + 1: a widget meant to sit over the picture needs a layer of at least `layer` + 2. Camera.lighting = "studio" lights it with its own key, fill and rim lights, wherever it stands. bloom and colorFilter of the camera are ignored (the frame has one set of post effects). A pointer press, drag, release and the wheel over it are the game event `ui.viewPointer` ({id, phase, x, y, u, v, dx, dy, wheel}; `ui.on("viewPointer", fn)` in scripts) so a script can turn what it shows. It is a widget for hit-testing (it blocks clicks to the world below it) but is not focusable. Costs one more render pass per view per frame, and the image per view: keep it as small as the picture needs (see `resolution`). Defaults: 320 x 240, no background colour.

Keeps HUD and buttons out of the notch. On a screen without cutouts (desktop, most tablets) it changes nothing. Default false (true on TouchStick and TouchButton). |
